items: Function attached to one field of one type
Returns the value for that field, nothing else
It resolves a FIELD — 'User resolver' is loose talk
One field, one job: not middleware, not a controller
Called once per parent object per request

blocks.text: The SDL declares shape and types; the map supplies behaviour. Two layers, glued at `makeExecutableSchema`/`buildSchema` time.

items: `Query`, `Mutation`, `Subscription` are plain object types

A field with no resolver is legal, not an error
Execution walks the query AST, one call per node

items: The value returned by the PARENT field's resolver

items: Coerced to schema types before your code runs

blocks.text: `parent` is the chain, `args` is the query, `context` is the request, `info` is the position.
Whatever a field's resolver returns becomes the `parent` of every resolver in that field's sub-selection. That is the entire mechanism.

blocks.text: Property reads beat function calls. Do not add resolvers you do not need.
